items.prompt: Which radical expression is equivalent to x^(3/4)?
items.explanation: In x^(m/n), the denominator n is the root index and the numerator m is the power, so x^(3/4) = ⁴√(x³).

commonErrors.why: Swapped the roles of numerator and denominator, using 3 as the root index and 4 as the power.
Treated the numerator 3 as a coefficient inside the radical instead of as a power of x.
Treated the numerator as a multiplier outside the radical instead of an exponent.

items.prompt: Which sum is an irrational number?
items.explanation: √5 is irrational, and the sum of a rational and an irrational number is irrational. The other sums combine rational numbers.

commonErrors.why: √36 = 6 is rational, so the sum is rational; the student assumed any square root is irrational.
√25 = 5 is rational, so the difference is rational; the student assumed any root is irrational.

items.explanation: √2 · √8 = √16 = 4, which is rational. Each other product is a nonzero rational times an irrational, which is always irrational.

commonErrors.why: A nonzero rational times an irrational is irrational, but the student thought it could be rational.
Same issue: 4 is rational and nonzero, √3 irrational, so the product is irrational.
Nonzero rational times irrational is irrational, not rational.

items.prompt: Which argument correctly shows that 1/2 + √3 is irrational?
items.explanation: Suppose 1/2 + √3 = r is rational. Then √3 = r − 1/2 is a difference of rationals, so rational, contradicting that √3 is irrational.
choices: Adding two numbers can only give a rational number when both are integers.
If it equaled a rational r, then √3 = r − 1/2 would be rational, which is false.
√3 has a never-ending decimal, so adding anything to it makes the sum never-ending.
The number 1/2 is smaller than √3, so the sum cannot be written as a fraction.
items.answer: If it equaled a rational r, then √3 = r − 1/2 would be rational, which is false.

commonErrors.answer: Adding two numbers can only give a rational number when both are integers.
commonErrors.why: Wrongly believes rational sums require integers; 1/2 + 1/2 = 1 and 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4.

commonErrors.answer: √3 has a never-ending decimal, so adding anything to it makes the sum never-ending.
commonErrors.why: Confused non-terminating with irrational: 1/3 also never ends but is rational.

commonErrors.answer: The number 1/2 is smaller than √3, so the sum cannot be written as a fraction.
commonErrors.why: Size comparison has no bearing on rationality.

items.subject: math
items.prompt: A club sells wristbands at price p dollars. Profit is P = (p − 4)(100 − 5p). In this expression, what does 100 − 5p represent?
items.explanation: Profit = (profit per item)(number sold). p − 4 is profit per item, so 100 − 5p is the number sold.
choices: The total revenue from all wristbands
The profit earned on each wristband sold
The cost the club pays per wristband
The number of wristbands sold at price p
items.answer: The number of wristbands sold at price p

commonErrors.answer: The total revenue from all wristbands
commonErrors.why: Revenue would be p(100 − 5p); this factor alone is not revenue.

commonErrors.answer: The profit earned on each wristband sold
commonErrors.why: Confused the number sold with the per-item profit p − 4.

commonErrors.answer: The cost the club pays per wristband
commonErrors.why: The per-item cost is the 4 subtracted in p − 4.

items.explanation: x² ≥ 0, so x² + 900 ≥ 900 and D ≥ 30, with D = 30 exactly when x = 0.
choices: D is never less than 30, because x² cannot be negative
D is always equal to x + 30 meters
D can be as small as 0 when x = 0
D gets smaller as x gets larger, since x is squared
